Population increased in Shropshire

The estimated population of Shropshire in 2024 was 332,455 usual residents, a rise of 0.9% since 2023.

This meant that Shropshire's rate of population change placed it about average among local authority districts in England and Wales.

In the period from mid-2021 to mid-2024, the population estimate of Shropshire increased by 2.4%.

Over this slightly longer period, Shropshire was also among the areas that had a broadly average population increase, of local authority districts in England and Wales.

Age profile of Shropshire

The average (median) age stayed at 48.9 years between 2023 and 2024.

You can see how the age profile of Shropshire has changed since 2011 in the population pyramid below.

sections.content:
Shropshire is an area that is classed as rural in nature according to the 2021 Census Rural Urban Classification.

By age category, Shropshire's population of 332,455 usual residents was made up of:

  • 52,320 people aged 0 to 15 years, (15.7%)
  • 192,339 people aged 16 to 64 years, (57.9%)
  • 87,796 people aged 65 years and over, (26.4%)

    • Compared with England and Wales as a whole, Shropshire has a higher proportion of people aged 65 years and over (26.4% compared with 18.9% for England and Wales).

Contributors to population change

We look at different flows of people into and out of areas and births and deaths to see what is driving population change in each area.

In Shropshire, the largest contribution to population change in the year to mid-2024 was from net internal migration.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Shropshire
sections.subtitle: How the population changed, by component

sections.content:
We estimate that, for Shropshire, between 2023 and 2024:

  • More deaths than births led to a fall in the population of 1,415 people (-0.4%). In total, there were 2,454 births and 3,869 deaths in Shropshire.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other areas in the UK) increased the population by 2,692 (0.8%). There were 15,228 people entering the area and 12,536 people leaving the area.
  • Net international migration led to an increase in Shropshire's population of 1,647 (0.5%) as a result of 2,480 people entering the area and 833 people leaving the area.
  • Other change (which includes changes to armed forces personnel and prisoners) for Shropshire was less than 0.1%.

Revisions to 2023 population estimates

We regularly revise our initial population estimates as we get more data and methods improve.

Our revised estimate for the population of Shropshire in mid-2023 is 329,558.

Within this, international migration was revised upwards by 466 people and internal migration estimates were revised downwards by 168 people.

Overall, there was an revision upwards of 298 people.
